note: The wire contract. The plugin is tested against this file: it asserts that it registered exactly the methods marked live, and that its codes and bounds are these. The Python tests check this file's own consistency, and will check the client against it when the socket transport lands. Prose lives in spec.md; this file is what the tests read.

parseError.doc: The line was not JSON. The connection survives; the line does not.

invalidRequest.doc: It was JSON, but not a request: a batch, a missing jsonrpc, an id that is neither a number nor a string, a second session.hello.

methodNotFound.doc: No method by that name. Nearly always a library newer than the plugin.

invalidParams.doc: The method exists; these arguments do not fit it. The library raises before the wire wherever it can, so this one arriving is a bug on one side or the other.

internalError.doc: A bug in the plugin. The message never carries what was thrown; the vault's console does. Nothing a caller can do about it, which is what OperationError means.

notFound.doc: A file, folder, command, leaf, handle or subscription that is not there.

alreadyExists.doc: Creating something that is already there.

conflict.doc: A compare-and-set lost its race: the file changed between the read and the commit.

unavailable.doc: The right request in the wrong application state: no active editor, a deferred leaf that will not load.

unauthenticated.doc: A method arrived before a valid handshake, or the proof did not match.

unsupportedProtocol.doc: No protocol major in common. The message names which side to update.

forbidden.doc: The capability this method needs is switched off in the plugin's settings. Its own class, because the answer is for a person to turn a switch on and no amount of retrying substitutes.

messageTooLarge.doc: A line longer than the frame cap, in either direction. A result over the cap names the paged alternative.

tooManyRequests.doc: Too many requests in flight on this connection. Its own class, because the answer is to wait for the answers already asked for.

cancelled.doc: The client withdrew the request. Delivered so a caller waiting on an id is never left waiting. It answers an rpc.cancel the caller sent and nothing else: the vault never withdraws a request on its own, so this code always arrives inside the call that asked for it, which is what makes asyncio.CancelledError the right class.

commands.doc: Running an arbitrary Obsidian command is code execution by proxy: it reaches every enabled plugin, including ones that talk to the network. Off unless the user turns it on.

unstable.doc: Methods and events that rest on undocumented Obsidian internals. They may break in any Obsidian release.

session.hello.summary: Prove the client may talk to this vault, and settle which protocol both speak.

protocol.doc: Every protocol major the client implements. The vault answers with the highest it shares.

proof.doc: HMAC-SHA256(token, nonce) as lowercase hex, over the nonce from session.challenge.

files.read.summary: Read a note as text, with the hash that makes a later write a compare-and-set.

files.create.summary: Create a note that is not there yet. The folder above it must already exist, and notFound is what says it does not.

files.write.summary: Write a note, creating it or replacing it whole. The folder above it must already exist, and notFound is what says it does not.

files.append.summary: Add to the end of a note without reading it first.

path.doc: Vault-relative path to an existing file.

content.doc: What to add, verbatim; no separator is inserted.

files.process.summary: Replace a note only if it still holds what was read: the commit half of read-modify-write.

path.doc: Vault-relative path to an existing file.

expect_hash.doc: The hash the read returned. Compared under the per-path lock; a mismatch is conflict and nothing is written.

files.delete.summary: Delete a file or folder, to the trash by default.

path.doc: Vault-relative path to a file or folder.

trash.doc: Where it goes: the operating system's trash, the vault's .trash folder, or nowhere at all.

files.move.summary: Move or rename a file or folder. Obsidian rewrites the links that pointed at it, note by note, after the move itself has landed; only the move is the atomic part.

path.doc: Vault-relative path to a file or folder.

to.doc: The new vault-relative path, including the name.

path.doc: Vault-relative path to a file or folder.

to.doc: The new vault-relative path, including the name.

files.create_folder.summary: Create a folder, and every folder above it that is missing.

files.exists.summary: Ask whether a path is there, and what it is.

files.stat.summary: Size and timestamps for one file or folder.

files.list.summary: List what is in a folder.

path.doc: Vault-relative folder path. Empty means the vault root.

kind.doc: Keep only files, only folders, or both.

extension.doc: Keep only files with this extension, without the dot.

files.read_binary.summary: Read one range of a file's bytes, so an attachment never travels as one frame.

length.doc: How many bytes to read. The vault reads a range, so it holds one chunk and not the file.

files.upload_begin.summary: Open a transactional binary write. Nothing appears at the path until it commits, so alreadyExists here is an early courtesy and not a promise: the path is checked again under the lock at commit, where the answer counts.

path.doc: Where the file will appear on commit.

overwrite.doc: Whether committing may replace a file that is already there.

files.upload_chunk.summary: Add bytes to an open upload.

files.upload_commit.summary: Put the uploaded file at its path, in one rename.

files.upload_abort.summary: Throw an upload away. The vault never saw it.

frontmatter.set.summary: Add, change and remove properties in one atomic write.

values.doc: Keys to write. A key already there is replaced; the rest of the block is left alone.

remove.doc: Keys to delete. A key that is not there is not an error.

values.doc: The properties the note will have. An empty object removes the block.

metadata.get.summary: Everything Obsidian's cache knows about one note: headings, tags, links, sections, list items, properties.

metadata.tags.summary: Every tag in the vault and how often it is used.

metadata.tagged.summary: The notes carrying a tag, read from the cache rather than by opening files.

tag.doc: The tag, with or without its leading #.

links.resolve.summary: Turn a link's text into a path, the way Obsidian would when following it.

name.doc: What is written inside the brackets.

from_path.doc: The note the link is written in, which decides what a relative name means.

links.outgoing.summary: The links leaving a note, resolved and unresolved alike.

links.backlinks.summary: The notes linking to this one.

links.unresolved.summary: Links that point at notes which do not exist.

path.doc: One note, or the whole vault when null.

links.format.summary: Write a link to a note the way this vault's settings say links are written.

from_path.doc: The note the link will be written in.

subpath.doc: A heading or block within the target, without the leading # or ^.

alias.doc: The text to display instead of the name.

pane.doc: Where it opens: over the current pane, in a new tab, beside it, or in its own window.

focus.doc: Whether the opened pane becomes the active one.

workspace.leaves.summary: Every open pane, with the id the editor methods take.

workspace.active_leaf.summary: The pane the user is in, or null when none is.

workspace.active_file.summary: The note the user is looking at, or null.

workspace.focus.summary: Bring a pane to the front and make it active.

workspace.recent_files.summary: The notes opened most recently, newest first.

editor.get.summary: What one editor holds right now: its text, its cursor and its selections.

leaf.doc: A leaf id, or null for the active markdown editor.

editor.set.summary: Replace everything in an editor, as one undoable edit.

leaf.doc: A leaf id, or null for the active markdown editor.

editor.replace.summary: Replace a range, or insert at a point when the range is empty.

from.doc: Where the replaced range starts. Null means the cursor.

to.doc: Where it ends. Null means the same place as from, which makes this an insert.

leaf.doc: A leaf id, or null for the active markdown editor.

editor.replace_selection.summary: Replace what is selected, or insert at the cursor when nothing is.

leaf.doc: A leaf id, or null for the active markdown editor.
A leaf id, or null for the active markdown editor.

head.doc: Where it is dragged to; this is where the cursor ends up.

leaf.doc: A leaf id, or null for the active markdown editor.

editor.exec.summary: Run one of the editor's own movement and folding commands.

command.doc: One of goUp, goDown, goLeft, goRight, goStart, goEnd, goWordLeft, goWordRight, indentMore, indentLess, newlineAndIndent, swapLineUp, swapLineDown, deleteLine, toggleFold, foldAll, unfoldAll.

leaf.doc: A leaf id, or null for the active markdown editor.

commands.list.summary: Every command Obsidian and its plugins have registered.

app.info.summary: What this vault is and what this plugin will do: versions, paths, and which capabilities are switched on.

app.plugins.summary: The community plugins installed here, and whether each is enabled.

app.config.summary: Read Obsidian's own settings. The result is an object keyed by setting name: one entry when key is given, every setting when it is not. A setting whose value is a bare number or boolean therefore still arrives inside an object.

key.doc: One setting, or every setting when null.

events.subscribe.summary: Start receiving events on this connection.

events.doc: The event names to receive. An unknown name is invalidParams, so a typo fails at once rather than silently delivering nothing, and so is gap, which is not subscribable: it arrives on every subscription whether asked for or not.

queue.doc: How many events may wait for a consumer that has stopped reading. Past it the oldest are dropped and a gap event says how many. Between 1 and 65536; anything else is invalidParams, because an unbounded queue is the renderer's memory spent by a peer that has stopped reading.

events.unsubscribe.summary: Stop receiving events. Closing the connection does this for every subscription on it.

session.challenge.summary: The first and only thing an unproven peer is told. Sent once, on accept.

nonce.doc: Thirty-two random bytes as lowercase hex.

session.goodbye.summary: Why the vault is hanging up, sent before it does.

reason.doc: Serving was switched off, or the plugin is being unloaded — which is Obsidian quitting, the vault closing and the plugin being disabled alike, because a plugin cannot tell those apart.

rpc.cancel.summary: Withdraw a request. The answer still arrives, as a cancelled error, so nothing waits forever.

id.doc: The id of the request being withdrawn.

events.event.summary: One event on one subscription. Events are ordered among themselves; responses may overtake them.

seq.doc: Counts from 1 within the subscription, gaps included.

event.doc: The event itself, discriminated by its name field.

file.created.summary: A file or folder appeared. Fires for every existing file when the vault is first indexed.

kind.doc: Whether it is a file or a folder.

file.modified.summary: A file's contents changed on disk.

path.doc: Vault-relative path of the file that changed.

file.deleted.summary: A file or folder went away.

path.doc: Vault-relative path of what went away.

kind.doc: Whether it was a file or a folder.

file.renamed.summary: A file or folder moved or was renamed.

kind.doc: Whether it is a file or a folder.

metadata.changed.summary: Obsidian re-read a note and its cache entry changed.

path.doc: The note whose cache entry changed.
The note that left the cache.

metadata.resolved.summary: Every link in the vault has been resolved; the link graph is settled.

path.doc: The note now on screen, or null when the pane holds no note.

workspace.layout_changed.summary: Panes were opened, closed or rearranged.

leaf.doc: The id of the pane now active, or null when none is.

path.doc: The note that pane holds, or null when it holds none.

unstable.raw.summary: A path under the vault's config directory changed: settings, themes, plugin state. This rests on an Obsidian event that is not in its public API and may vanish in any release.

path.doc: The path under the config directory that changed.

gap.summary: Events were dropped because the consumer stopped reading. Delivered in order, in the stream, so the decision to re-read state is made where the events are read.

missed.doc: How many events were dropped, counted in this subscription's own sequence numbers.

protocol.doc: The major both sides settled on, and the vault's exact minor.

server_proof.doc: HMAC-SHA256(token, nonce ‖ "s") as lowercase hex. The client verifies it before sending any note content.

plugin_version.doc: The plugin's own version, from its manifest.

obsidian_version.doc: The Obsidian API version the plugin is running against.

vault.doc: Which vault answered. Untrusted: every field is whatever the peer said.

major.doc: A break. A client that does not implement it is refused.

id.doc: Sixteen hex characters derived from the vault's real path. A name, not a secret.

path.doc: Where it sits, resolved through realpath. Never fed back into local filesystem work.

hash.doc: SHA-256 over the exact bytes, lowercase hex. Hand it to files.process to write only if nothing changed.
SHA-256 of what is now on disk, so a caller can chain writes without re-reading.

extension.doc: Without the dot; null for folders and for files that have none.
Without the dot; null for folders and for files that have none.

created.doc: Milliseconds since the epoch, as the operating system reports it.

exists.doc: Whether anything is at that path.

kind.doc: What it is, or null when nothing is there.

length.doc: How many bytes it holds, which may be fewer than asked for.

size.doc: The whole file's size, so a caller knows how far it has to go.

eof.doc: Whether this chunk reaches the end.

handle.doc: Names this upload until it commits or is thrown away.

written.doc: Bytes written to the temporary file so far.

properties.doc: The property block as YAML would parse it. Empty when the note has none.

frontmatter.doc: The property block, or null when the note has none.

frontmatter_position.doc: Where the block sits in the file.

sections.doc: Root-level blocks, which is how the document divides up.

list_items.doc: Every list item, with its nesting and its task state.

footnotes.doc: Footnote definitions. Obsidian has reported these since 1.6.6.

footnote_refs.doc: Footnote references. Obsidian has reported these since 1.8.7.

line.doc: Zero-based, as Obsidian counts. Not translated: these feed straight back into editor calls.

offset.doc: Characters from the start of the file.

link.doc: What is written inside the brackets, before any alias.

original.doc: The whole link, exactly as it appears in the file.

display_text.doc: The alias, when there is one.

key.doc: The property the link is written in.

link.doc: What is written inside the brackets.

original.doc: The whole link, as it appears.

display_text.doc: The alias, when there is one.

type.doc: blockquote, callout, code, heading, list, paragraph, table, yaml and the rest; Obsidian may add more.

id.doc: The block id, when the section carries one.

parent.doc: The line of the item this one sits under; negative at the top level.

task.doc: What is between the brackets of a checkbox — a space when unchecked, x when checked — or null when the item is not a task.

id.doc: The block id, when the item carries one.

count.doc: How many times it is used across the vault.

resolved.doc: Links that point at a note which exists.

count.doc: How many links point there from the source.

from_path.doc: The note the link is written in.

link.doc: The name that resolves to nothing.

count.doc: How many times it appears there.
How many of its links point here.

id.doc: Obsidian's own id for the pane. Stable while the pane is open, and nothing more.

view_type.doc: markdown, graph, canvas, and whatever plugins register.

path.doc: The file it shows, when it shows one.

active.doc: Whether this is the pane the user is in.

group.doc: The link group it belongs to, when it belongs to one.

head.doc: Where it is dragged to; this is where the cursor is.

leaf.doc: The pane this editor belongs to.

content.doc: The whole document, which is what is on screen and may differ from what is on disk.

selections.doc: Every selection, because Obsidian allows more than one.

line_count.doc: How many lines the document has.

icon.doc: The icon name, when the command has one.

capabilities.doc: Each capability name to whether it is switched on, so a caller learns what is gated without provoking a refusal.

subscription.doc: Names this subscription on this connection.

name.doc: Which event this is: one of the names in the events table. The rest of the object is that event's own fields, flattened in beside this one, which is why no event may declare a field called name.
